title: pravapis rule file
description: A declarative orthography rule file (data/rules/*.yaml). NORMATIVE: an implementation in any language reads this schema, not src/pravapis/rules/engine.py. Rules are applied in descending priority order for the requested direction, ties broken by id; `repeat` rules are then re-run together until the word stops changing. The behavioural contract is conformance/cases.jsonl.

direction.description: The orthography a rule PRODUCES. The long forms name both endpoints and are preferred; the short forms are accepted aliases naming the target only.

alternation.description: An alternation code a loan stem may license, as declared in stems.schema.json: l = soft л, i = і→ы, e = е→э, g = г→ґ, eu = еў→эў.

rule.description: One rule. Exactly one of 'pattern' or 'function' must be present.

id.description: Stable identifier, reported in every change record as `rule`. Dotted namespace: group.name[.qualifier].

description.description: What the rule does, in prose, for a reader checking it against the codification.

citation.description: Where the rule comes from, and it must come from somewhere. Either a place in the codification ('Збор 2005, §55.1'), or 'derived:<rule-id>' when the rule is the inverse of another — optionally carrying the section the pair rests on, 'derived:palat.assim (Збор 2005, §29)' — or 'convention:<short reason>' for a spelling the codification does not legislate. Surfaced on every change record as `citation`, which is why it is required: a change a caller cannot trace is a change they have to take on faith.

pattern.description: A regular expression applied to the lowercased word. Portability: ports must support the constructs used here — non-capturing groups, lookahead, lookbehind, alternation, and numbered backreferences in `replacement`. No flags are set externally; write any inline.

replacement.description: Substitution template for `pattern`. Backreferences are written \1, \2 … Only meaningful with `pattern`.

function.description: A named transformation the host implements, referenced as 'module:callable'. The escape hatch for transducers a regex cannot express — chiefly rewrites bounded to the matched stem span. A port MUST reimplement the named behaviour; the conformance corpus is what pins it down.

priority.description: Higher runs first. The etymology rules sit above palatalization (which tops out at 120): softness is a consequence of the vowel, so the vowel has to be settled first.

repeat.description: Re-apply until the word stops changing (bounded at 8 passes), for softness that chains across a word.

optional.description: The codification permits both the input and the output form. Applied only in aggressive mode; off by default.

requires.description: Rule ids that must already have fired on this word. Must name rules of the same direction; cycles are rejected.

exceptions.description: Whole words (lowercased) the rule must leave alone.

requires_class.description: Fire only on a word whose longest matched stem has this etymology class, per stems.schema.json. This gate is what keeps план → плян from also producing лапа → ляпа.

alternation.description: …and only if that stem licenses this alternation. Requires `requires_class`.

tests.description: Inline cases, exported verbatim into the conformance corpus. A positive case must change as given; a negative case must come back unchanged.

allOf.title: A rule without a `function` must carry a `pattern`
…and a rule with one must not carry both

then.title: Flat layout (accepted)
then.description: A bare list of rules, each stating its own direction.

else.title: Grouped layout (preferred)
else.description: One group of rules per file, with a shared default direction.

version.description: Schema generation this file is written against, major.minor. Distinct from data/VERSION, which versions the content.

group.description: Name of the rule group; matches the file stem.

direction.description: Default direction for rules in this file that do not state one.
